title: Choose the visual world for the land assistant
question: The roll assigned the banknote-and-stamp world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Dinar & Timbre
options.lineage: Tunisian dinar notes and postage stamps
options.thesis: Land is priced and stamped the way Tunisians already read official value: banknote inks, bilingual figures, a postmark on every confirmed request.
options.viewport: Violet band with the bilingual name; conversation left, map and plots right; amounts set as denominations; confirming franks the draft with a bilingual postmark.
options.risk: Guilloché used everywhere becomes a costume; it must stay on the official moments only.

raised.raise: Zones and plots are flat, unmodulated colour fields: no gradients, no shadows.
Every lot and request carries its serial id as its primary handle, set like a banknote serial.
Three inks plus paper, and every rule a single hairline.
Selecting a lot lifts it and dims the rest, on the map and the plan alike.
All figures are tabular, so prices and areas compare at a glance.

options.label: Panneau / لافتة
options.thesis: Finding where your factory goes is wayfinding: bilingual panels point the investor to the zone.
options.viewport: Blue header panel, Arabic and French labels stacked like a sign; the answer arrives with a direction panel naming the matching zones.
options.risk: Familiar wayfinding grammar; at laptop density it can swell into oversized labels.

options.label: Ticket wallet
options.thesis: A request is a coupon book: search, draft and confirmation tear off in sequence and stamp their own state.
options.viewport: The conversation beside a coupon stack: each found lot a coupon, the draft a validated coupon, a sold lot stamped void.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and states read very clearly, but investors identify less with airline paper than with their own banknotes.
options.risk: Can read as travel-themed if the coupons are not tied tightly to land.

options.label: Guide map
options.thesis: Zones as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.viewport: One zone lobe owns the screen.
options.risk: Playful leisure map for a serious purchase.
options.case: Loses both axes: investors do not read land as a day out.
options.kept: Flat, unmodulated colour fields for zones and plots.

options.label: Factory catalogue
options.thesis: Every artefact gets a catalogue number.
options.viewport: A coded index as the only map.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded state fights clarity.
options.kept: Serial ids as the primary handle.

options.label: Reference setting
options.thesis: Two columns around a rail of keys.
options.risk: A reading surface, not a task surface.
options.case: Loses both axes for an operating screen.
options.kept: Three inks plus paper; hairline rules only.

options.label: Title wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles; the focused one grows.
options.risk: Entertainment browsing for a regulated purchase.
options.kept: Selection lifts one item and dims the rest.

options.label: Data field
options.thesis: Barcode columns in pure black and white.
options.kept: Tabular figures for every price and area.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean AI-assistant workspace: chat panel, map, neutral greys and one blue accent, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Chat on the left, map on the right, everything where a SaaS user expects it.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other AI assistant by design.
